title.zh: 卷284 列傳七十一 觉史满保 施世骠 蓝廷珍 林亮 欧阳凯
title.en: Volume 284 Biographies 71: Jue Shi Man Bao, Shi Shibiao, Lan Tingzhen, Lin Liang, Ou Yangkai
title.raw: 卷284 列傳七十一 觉史满保 施世骠 蓝廷珍 林亮 欧阳凯

sentences.zh: 列傳七十一

translations.literal: Biographies 71
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 71

sentences.zh: 覺羅滿保陳策施世驃藍廷珍從弟鼎元林亮何勉陳倫炯

translations.literal: Aisin-Gioro Manbao, Chen Ce, Shi Shibiao, Lan Tingzhen, his younger cousin Ding Yuan, Lin Liang, He Mian, Chen Lunjiong
translations.idiomatic: Aisin-Gioro Manbao, Chen Ce, Shi Shibiao, Lan Tingzhen, his younger cousin Ding Yuan, Lin Liang, He Mian, and Chen Lunjiong

sentences.zh: 歐陽凱羅萬倉遊崇功

translations.literal: Ouyang Kai, Luo Wancang, You Chonggong
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Kai, Luo Wancang, and You Chonggong

sentences.zh: 覺羅滿保，字鳧山，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Aisin-Gioro Manbao, style name Fushan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Aisin-Gioro Manbao, whose style name was Fushan, came from the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十三年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the thirty-third year of the Kangxi reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子監祭酒，擢內閣學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, then elevated to Grand Secretariat academician and served on the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, was then promoted to Grand Secretariat academician, and attended the imperial lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 五十年，授福建巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was appointed Fujian governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 疏言福州、興化、泉、漳等屬十六州縣皆瀕海要地，請揀選直省卓異官除授。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the sixteen prefectures and counties under Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and the like were all vital coastal places, and requested that outstanding officials from other provinces be selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial stating that the sixteen prefectures and counties under Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and related jurisdictions were all critical coastal posts, and asked that distinguished officials from other provinces be chosen for appointment there.

sentences.zh: 御史璩廷祜論其不可，部議以為然。

translations.literal: Censor Qu Tingyou argued that this could not be done; the ministry deliberation agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qu Tingyou objected that the proposal was unworkable, and the ministry concurred.

sentences.zh: 詔下九卿等再議，卒從滿保言。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Nine Ministers and others to deliberate again; in the end Manbao's view was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Nine Ministers and others to reconsider, and in the end adopted Manbao's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，擢福建浙江總督，命巡海。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang and ordered to patrol the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was elevated to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang and charged with maritime patrol.

sentences.zh: 議自乍浦至南澳，沿海五千餘裡，建台、寨百二十七所，砲位千一百七十有八。

translations.literal: It was proposed that from Zhapu to Nan'ao, along more than five thousand li of coast, one hundred twenty-seven forts and stockades and one thousand one hundred seventy-eight gun emplacements be built.
translations.idiomatic: A plan was drawn up to build one hundred twenty-seven forts and stockades and one thousand one hundred seventy-eight gun emplacements along the more than five thousand li of coast from Zhapu to Nan'ao.

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「鹿耳門為台灣咽喉，澎湖為廈門籓衛，安平鎮為水師三營重地，及海洋各口岸宜分極衝、次沖，築墩、台，設汛巡守；

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: "Luer Men is the throat of Taiwan; Penghu is the outer defense of Xiamen; Anping Town is a key post of the three naval camps; and the various maritime ports should be divided into highest and secondary priority points of attack, with mounds and towers built and garrison patrols established;
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he wrote: "Luer Men is the gateway of Taiwan, Penghu is the shield of Xiamen, Anping is a vital station of the three naval camps, and the various sea ports should be ranked by priority of threat, with redoubts and towers built and patrol garrisons stationed there;

sentences.zh: 並嚴察海船出入，禁漁船私載米糧、軍器。

translations.literal: and sea vessels entering and leaving should be strictly inspected, and fishing boats forbidden to carry grain or weapons privately."
translations.idiomatic: sea traffic should be strictly inspected, and fishing boats barred from secretly carrying grain or arms."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「淡水、雞籠山為台灣北界，其澳港可泊巨艦百餘。

translations.literal: He also said: "Tamsui and Jilong Mountain mark Taiwan's northern boundary; its bays and harbors can moor more than a hundred large warships.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Tamsui and Jilong Mountain form Taiwan's northern frontier; its bays can anchor more than a hundred large warships.

sentences.zh: 更進為肩豆門，沃野百里，番社交據。

translations.literal: Farther north is Gandou Gate, with a hundred li of fertile land where aboriginal communities alternate in occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Farther on lies Gandou Gate, where a hundred li of fertile plain is held in turn by aboriginal communities.

sentences.zh: 請增置淡水營，設官駐防為後蔽。

translations.literal: He requested that a Tamsui garrison be added and officials stationed there as a rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a Tamsui garrison be established with officials posted there to secure the rear.

sentences.zh: 」皆報可。

translations.literal: "All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: "All of these proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 六十年，鳳山民硃一貴為亂。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the Fengshan commoner Zhu Yigui raised a rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi, Zhu Yigui, a man of Fengshan, led a revolt.

sentences.zh: 台灣知府王珍苛稅濫刑，鳳山民黃殿、李勇、吳外等集數百人謀變，一貴素販鴨，託明裔以為渠。

translations.literal: The Taiwan prefect Wang Zhen imposed harsh taxes and arbitrary punishments; the Fengshan men Huang Dian, Li Yong, Wu Wai, and others gathered several hundred men to plot rebellion; Yigui had sold ducks for a living and passed himself off as a Ming descendant to serve as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiwan prefect Wang Zhen levied crushing taxes and arbitrary punishments. Huang Dian, Li Yong, Wu Wai, and other men of Fengshan gathered several hundred followers to plot an uprising. Yigui, who had made his living selling ducks, claimed Ming imperial descent and was made their leader.

sentences.zh: 劫岡山塘、檳榔林二汛，掠軍器，眾益聚，遂破縣城，進陷台灣。

translations.literal: They raided the Gangshan Pond and Betel Grove garrisons, seized weapons, and as the crowd grew they broke the county seat and advanced to seize Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked the Gangshan Pond and Betel Grove outposts, seized arms, and as their numbers swelled they stormed the county seat and overran Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 總兵歐陽凱等率兵禦賊，師敗績，死之。

translations.literal: Regional commander Ouyang Kai and others led troops to resist the rebels; the army was defeated and they died.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Ouyang Kai led the army against the rebels, was defeated, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 台廈道梁文煊等走澎湖。

translations.literal: The Taiwan-Xiamen intendant Liang Wenxuan and others fled to Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiwan-Xiamen intendant Liang Wenxuan and others retreated to Penghu.

sentences.zh: 滿保疏聞，督兵趨廈門，值淫雨，乘竹兜從數騎行泥淖中。

translations.literal: Manbao reported by memorial, led troops toward Xiamen, encountered heavy rain, and rode a bamboo sedan with a few horsemen through the mud.
translations.idiomatic: Manbao reported the crisis and hurried troops to Xiamen. Torrential rains forced him to travel in a bamboo sedan with only a few mounted escorts through the mud.

sentences.zh: 比至，籍丁壯剽悍能殺賊者悉充伍，嚴申軍令，禁舟師毋登陸，民以不擾。

translations.literal: When he arrived he enrolled all able-bodied fierce men who could kill rebels into the ranks, strictly enforced military orders, forbade the fleet to go ashore, and the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he enrolled every able-bodied man bold enough to fight into the ranks, enforced strict discipline, forbade naval troops to land ashore, and thereby kept the populace from being harassed.

sentences.zh: 淡水營守備陳策使詣廈門乞援，滿保移會巡撫呂猶龍，遣兵自閩安渡淡水。

translations.literal: Tamsui garrison commandant Chen Ce sent an envoy to Xiamen to beg for aid; Manbao notified Governor Lü Youlong and dispatched troops from Min'an across to Tamsui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ce, commandant of the Tamsui garrison, sent an envoy to Xiamen pleading for reinforcements. Manbao coordinated with Governor Lü Youlong and sent troops from Min'an across to Tamsui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南澳鎮總兵藍廷珍率舟師至，滿保命統水陸軍，會提督施世驃於澎湖，剋期進剿。

translations.literal: Before long Nan'ao regional commander Lan Tingzhen arrived with the fleet; Manbao ordered him to command the combined land and sea forces, joined Provincial Military Commissioner Shi Shibiao at Penghu, and set a date for the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nan'ao regional commander Lan Tingzhen arrived with the fleet. Manbao placed him in command of the combined land and sea forces, joined Provincial Military Commissioner Shi Shibiao at Penghu, and fixed a date for the assault.

sentences.zh: 六月，世驃、廷珍攻鹿耳門，敗賊安平鎮，遂克台灣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Shi Shibiao and Lan Tingzhen attacked Luer Men, defeated the rebels at Anping Town, and then recovered Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Shi Shibiao and Lan Tingzhen attacked Luer Men, routed the rebels at Anping, and recovered Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 上以台灣民附亂非本意，敕滿保招撫。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that the people of Taiwan had joined the rebellion not of their own intent, ordered Manbao to offer amnesty and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that most Taiwanese had joined the revolt unwillingly and ordered Manbao to offer amnesty and pacification.

sentences.zh: 尋諸羅民楊旭等密約壯丁六百人，擒一貴及其黨十二人，獻世驃軍前，檻送京師，磔於市。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter the Zhuluo man Yang Xu and others secretly gathered six hundred able-bodied men, captured Yigui and twelve of his partisans, presented them before Shi Shibiao's army, sent them in a caged cart to the capital, and they were dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the men of Zhuluo, led by Yang Xu, secretly mustered six hundred strong men, seized Yigui and twelve of his lieutenants, and delivered them to Shi Shibiao's camp. They were sent to the capital in cages and executed by dismemberment in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 是役，自出師迄事平凡七日。

translations.literal: In this campaign, from dispatch of troops until completion of affairs, it was only seven days.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening of the campaign to its conclusion took only seven days.

sentences.zh: 上嘉滿保調度有方，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Manbao's well-ordered command and added to him the rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Manbao's skillful coordination and promoted him to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「賊起，惟守備陳策鼓勵兵民，堅守汛地，待大兵進援，奮力效忠。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "When the rebels rose, only commandant Chen Ce encouraged soldiers and civilians, held firm at the garrison post, awaited the advance of the main army, and strove with loyal effort."
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized: "When the rebellion broke out, only Commandant Chen Ce rallied soldiers and civilians, held his garrison post, awaited the main army's relief, and fought with devoted loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」命擢台灣總兵。

translations.literal: "He was ordered promoted to Taiwan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered promoted to regional commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 复疏劾珍縱役需索，致一貴乘機倡亂；

translations.literal: He again memorialized to impeach Wang Zhen for allowing runners to extort demands, causing Yigui to seize the opportunity to incite rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Wang Zhen for letting his runners extort the people, giving Yigui his opening to incite rebellion;

sentences.zh: 文煊及所屬官吏一無備禦，退回澎湖，應奪官逮問，從之，文煊等論罪如律。

translations.literal: Wenxuan and the officials under him made no defense whatsoever and retreated to Penghu; they should be stripped of office and arrested for inquiry — this was approved, and Wenxuan and others were sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: and charged that Wenxuan and his subordinates had made no defense and fled to Penghu, for which they should be dismissed and arrested. The court agreed, and Wenxuan and the others were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 秋，台灣颶作，滿保以聞，諭：「台灣有司平日貪殘激變，及大兵進剿，殺戮之氣上乾天和，令速行賑恤。

translations.literal: In autumn a typhoon struck Taiwan; Manbao reported it, and was instructed: "The Taiwan officials were greedy and cruel in ordinary times and provoked rebellion; when the great army advanced to suppress them, the aura of slaughter offended Heaven's harmony — order swift relief and succor."
translations.idiomatic: That autumn a typhoon struck Taiwan. Manbao reported it and received this instruction: "Taiwan's officials were greedy and cruel in peacetime and provoked rebellion; when the army marched in, the killing offended Heaven's harmony. Provide relief at once."

sentences.zh: 上杭民溫上貴往台灣從一貴得偽元帥札、印，還上杭，煽鄉人從賊。

translations.literal: The Shanghang man Wen Shanggui went to Taiwan, followed Yigui, obtained a false marshal's dispatch and seal, returned to Shanghang, and incited villagers to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shanggui of Shanghang went to Taiwan, joined Yigui's cause, obtained forged marshal credentials and a seal, returned home, and incited his neighbors to rebel.

sentences.zh: 聞一貴誅，走江西，結棚匪數百，謀掠萬載。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yigui had been executed, he fled to Jiangxi, gathered several hundred shed-bandits, and plotted to plunder Wanzai.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Yigui had been executed, he fled to Jiangxi, rallied several hundred shed-dweller bandits, and plotted to raid Wanzai.

sentences.zh: 知縣施昭庭集營汛剿捕，擒上貴及其黨十數人，並伏法。

translations.literal: Magistrate Shi Zhaoting gathered garrison troops to pursue and capture them, seized Shanggui and more than ten of his partisans, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Shi Zhaoting mobilized garrison troops, captured Shanggui and more than ten of his followers, and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 大學士白潢等條奏禁戢棚匪，滿保疏言：「閩、浙兩省棚民，以種麻靛、造紙、燒灰為業，良莠不一。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Bai Huang and others submitted detailed memorials to suppress shed-bandits; Manbao memorialized: "In Fujian and Zhejiang the shed-dwellers make their living growing indigo, making paper, and burning lime — good and bad are mixed."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Bai Huang and others proposed measures to suppress shed-banditry. Manbao wrote: "In Fujian and Zhejiang, shed-dwellers earn their living growing indigo, making paper, and burning lime, and the honest and the criminal live side by side."

sentences.zh: 令鄰坊保結，棚長若有容庇匪類，依律連坐。

translations.literal: Let neighboring wards and hamlets be bound in collective responsibility; if a shed chief harbors bandits, he shall be punished by joint liability according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring wards and hamlets should be bound in collective responsibility, and any shed chief who harbors criminals should be punished by joint liability under the law.

sentences.zh: 有司於農隙遍履各棚，嚴加稽察。

translations.literal: Officials in the agricultural slack season should visit every shed and conduct strict inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials should inspect every shed during the agricultural off-season and enforce strict surveillance.

sentences.zh: 浙江鄞、奉化等二十七縣，福建閩、龍巖等四十州縣，皆有棚民，宜如沿海州縣例，揀員題補。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang's Yin, Fenghua, and twenty-seven other counties, and Fujian's Min, Longyan, and forty other prefectures and counties, there are all shed-dwellers; officials should be selected and nominated for appointment as in the coastal counties.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven counties in Zhejiang, including Yin and Fenghua, and forty prefectures and counties in Fujian, including Min and Longyan, all have shed-dwellers. Officials should be selected and appointed there by the same standards used for coastal posts.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: "An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the third year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言：「新任巡撫毛文銓未至，總督印信交福州將軍宜兆熊署理，並留解任巡撫黃國材暫緩起程，如舊辦事。

translations.literal: His final memorial said: "The newly appointed governor Mao Wenquan has not yet arrived; the governor-general's seal should be entrusted to Fuzhou General Yi Zhaoxiong to act in his stead, and the dismissed governor Huang Guocai should be kept from departing for the time being to conduct affairs as before."
translations.idiomatic: In his deathbed memorial he wrote: "The newly appointed governor Mao Wenquan has not yet arrived. The governor-general's seal should be entrusted to Fuzhou General Yi Zhaoxiong, and the outgoing governor Huang Guocai should remain briefly to continue routine administration."

sentences.zh: 」詔嘉其得體，下部議血阝；

translations.literal: "An edict praised his propriety and ordered the ministries to deliberate on posthumous honors;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his tact and ordered the ministries to deliberate on posthumous honors;

sentences.zh: 時尚書隆科多獲罪鞫訊，得滿保餽金交通狀，世宗諭責滿保諂隆科多、年羹堯，命毋賜卹予諡。

translations.literal: At that time Minister Longkedo was convicted and interrogated, and evidence was obtained of Manbao's gifts of gold and dealings with him; the Yongzheng Emperor rebuked Manbao for fawning on Longkedo and Nian Gengyao and ordered that no posthumous gifts or posthumous title be granted.
translations.idiomatic: But when Minister Longkedo was tried for crimes, evidence surfaced of Manbao's gifts of gold and dealings with him. The Yongzheng Emperor rebuked Manbao for currying favor with Longkedo and Nian Gengyao and ordered that no posthumous honors or title be granted.

sentences.zh: 策，字鍾侯，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Ce, style name Zhonghou, was a man of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ce, whose style name was Zhonghou, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由銅山守備調淡水。

translations.literal: He was transferred from Tongshan commandant to Tamsui.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from commandant at Tongshan to Tamsui.

sentences.zh: 一貴陷台灣，策孤軍力守一隅。

translations.literal: When Yigui seized Taiwan, Ce with a lone army strove to hold one corner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yigui overran Taiwan, Chen Ce held his post alone with a single detachment.

sentences.zh: 奸人苑景文入境煽誘，擒誅之。

translations.literal: The traitor Yuan Jingwen entered the territory to incite and entice; Ce captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the traitor Yuan Jingwen crossed the border to incite rebellion, Chen Ce seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 師下台灣，滿保檄剿北路，复南嵌、竹塹、中港、後壟、吞霄、大甲諸社。

translations.literal: When the army descended on Taiwan, Manbao ordered him to suppress the northern route and recover the communities of Nanqian, Zhuqian, Zhonggang, Houlong, Tunxiao, Dajia, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial forces landed in Taiwan, Manbao ordered him to pacify the northern route and recover Nanqian, Zhuqian, Zhonggang, Houlong, Tunxiao, Dajia, and other aboriginal settlements.

sentences.zh: 以功擢台灣總兵，加左都督。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Taiwan regional commander and given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to regional commander of Taiwan and given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 施世驃，字文秉，靖海侯瑯第六子。

translations.literal: Shi Shibiao, style name Wenbing, was the sixth son of Marquis Jinghai Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shibiao, whose style name was Wenbing, was the sixth son of Marquis Jinghai Shi Lang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十二年，世驃年十五，從瑯下台灣，委署守備。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, Shibiao at age fifteen followed Lang in the descent on Taiwan and was appointed acting commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, when Shibiao was fifteen, he followed his father in the conquest of Taiwan and was appointed acting commandant.

sentences.zh: 台灣既定，以功加左都督銜，授山東濟南城守參將。

translations.literal: After Taiwan was pacified, for merit he was given the nominal rank of Left Commander-in-Chief and appointed garrison deputy commander of Jinan City in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified, he was given the nominal rank of Left Commander-in-Chief for his service and appointed deputy garrison commander of Jinan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，聖祖親征噶爾丹，天津總兵岳昇龍薦世驃從軍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the Sacred Ancestor personally campaigned against Galdan; Tianjin regional commander Yue Shenglong recommended Shibiao to join the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year the Kangxi Emperor campaigned in person against Galdan, and Tianjin regional commander Yue Shenglong recommended Shibiao for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 召試騎射，命護糧運至奎素，從大將軍馬斯喀追賊至巴顏烏闌。

translations.literal: He was summoned to test mounted archery, ordered to escort grain transport to Kuisu, and followed Grand General Fiyanggū in pursuit of the enemy to Bayan Ulan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to demonstrate his horsemanship and archery, ordered to escort grain convoys to Kuisu, and followed Grand General Fiyanggū in pursuit of the enemy to Bayan Ulan.

sentences.zh: 師還，假歸葬。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was granted leave to return home for a funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was granted leave to go home for a funeral.

sentences.zh: 上褒世驃勤勞，命事畢仍還任。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Shibiao's diligent service and ordered that when the matter was finished he should still return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Shibiao's diligence and ordered him to resume his post when the funeral was complete.

sentences.zh: 累遷浙江定海總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to regional commander of Dinghai in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to regional commander of Dinghai in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，賜御書「彰信敦禮」榜。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, during the emperor's southern tour, he was granted an imperial inscription reading "Manifest Faith and Cultivate Rites."
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, during the emperor's southern tour, he received an imperial plaque inscribed "Manifest Faith and Cultivate Rites."

sentences.zh: 時海中多盜，世驃屢出洋巡緝，先遣裨將假商船餌盜，擒獲甚眾，斬盜渠江崙。

translations.literal: At the time pirates were numerous at sea; Shibiao repeatedly went out on patrol, first sending deputy generals in merchant ships as bait for pirates, capturing very many, and beheading the pirate chieftain Jiang Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates were then rampant at sea. Shibiao patrolled repeatedly, first sending deputies disguised aboard merchant ships to lure them out, captured large numbers, and beheaded the pirate leader Jiang Lun.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上南巡，詢及擒斬海盜事，溫諭嘉獎，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, during the southern tour, the emperor inquired about the capture and beheading of pirates, gave warm praise and reward, and bestowed a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year, on another southern tour, the emperor asked about his capture of pirates, praised him warmly, and bestowed a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，擢廣東提督。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to Guangdong provincial military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to provincial military commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，調福建水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was transferred to Fujian naval provincial military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was transferred to provincial military commissioner of the Fujian naval forces.

sentences.zh: 六十年，硃一貴為亂，陷台灣。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Zhu Yigui rebelled and seized Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year Zhu Yigui rebelled and overran Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 世驃聞報，即率所部進扼澎湖，總督滿保檄南澳總兵藍廷珍等以師會。

translations.literal: On hearing the report Shibiao immediately led his command to advance and hold Penghu; Governor-General Manbao ordered Nan'ao regional commander Lan Tingzhen and others to join forces.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news Shibiao immediately led his troops to seize Penghu, while Governor-General Manbao ordered Nan'ao regional commander Lan Tingzhen and others to join him.

sentences.zh: 眾議三路進攻。

translations.literal: The assembly debated a three-route attack.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders debated a three-pronged assault.

sentences.zh: 世驃謂南路打狗港在台灣正南，南風盛，不可泊；

translations.literal: Shibiao said the southern route at Dagou Harbor lay due south of Taiwan, where south winds were strong and anchorage was impossible;
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao argued that the southern route through Dagou Harbor lay due south of Taiwan, where strong southerly winds made anchorage impossible;

sentences.zh: 北路清風隙去府百餘裡，運餉艱；

translations.literal: the northern route at Qingfeng Gap was more than a hundred li from the prefectural seat and supply transport was difficult;
translations.idiomatic: that the northern route at Qingfeng Gap was more than a hundred li from the prefectural seat and supply lines would be arduous;

sentences.zh: 度賊必屯聚中路，宜直搗鹿耳門。

translations.literal: he judged the rebels would certainly mass on the central route, and it was fitting to strike straight at Luer Men.
translations.idiomatic: and that the rebels would surely mass on the central route, so the army should strike directly at Luer Men.

sentences.zh: 時台地諸將吏皆退次澎湖，惟淡水守備陳策堅守汛地。

translations.literal: At that time all Taiwan generals and officials had withdrawn to Penghu; only Tamsui commandant Chen Ce held firm at his garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: By then every Taiwan officer had retreated to Penghu except Tamsui commandant Chen Ce, who still held his garrison post.

sentences.zh: 世驃遣游擊張駴等赴援，自統師出中路。

translations.literal: Shibiao sent brigade commander Zhang Chi and others to relieve him and personally commanded the army on the central route.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao sent Brigade Commander Zhang Chi and others to relieve him and personally led the main force on the central route.

sentences.zh: 選勁卒，乘小舟，載旗幟，分伏南北港。

translations.literal: He selected crack troops, boarded small boats carrying banners, and stationed them in ambush at the northern and southern harbors.
translations.idiomatic: He chose crack troops, sent them in small boats bearing banners, and stationed them in ambush at the northern and southern harbors.

sentences.zh: 六月，抵鹿耳門。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they reached Luer Men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they reached Luer Men.

sentences.zh: 賊踞砲台以拒。

translations.literal: The rebels held the gun batteries to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the batteries and resisted.

sentences.zh: 世驃登樓船督戰，發砲中敵貯火藥器，火大熾，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Shibiao boarded a tower ship to direct the battle, fired cannon that struck the enemy's powder stores, the fire blazed fiercely, and the rebels fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao boarded a tower ship to direct the battle. His cannon struck the enemy's powder stores, the blaze roared up, and the rebels broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 眾軍齊進，兩港悉樹我軍幟。

translations.literal: All armies advanced together, and both harbors raised our banners.
translations.idiomatic: The whole fleet pressed forward, and imperial banners rose at both harbors.

sentences.zh: 賊不敢犯，揚帆直渡鯤身。

translations.literal: The rebels dared not attack and set sail straight across Kun Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dared not engage and sailed straight across the Kun Shen shoals.

sentences.zh: 鯤身者海沙也，水淺，大舟不能過。

translations.literal: Kun Shen is sea sand; the water is shallow and large ships cannot pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kun Shen is a sandbar; the water is shallow and large ships cannot cross it.

sentences.zh: 是日海水驟漲八尺餘，舟乘風疾上，遂克安平鎮。

translations.literal: That day the sea water suddenly rose more than eight chi, the boats rode the wind swiftly forward, and they then captured Anping Town.
translations.idiomatic: That day the tide surged more than eight feet, the fleet rode the wind across, and Anping fell.

sentences.zh: 翌日，戰，破賊。

translations.literal: The next day they fought and defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊悉眾來犯，世驃遣守備林亮等進西港，游擊硃文等越七鯤身，自鹽埕、大井頭分道登陸趨台灣。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered all their forces to attack; Shibiao sent commandant Lin Liang and others to advance on Xigang, brigade commander Zhu Wen and others crossed the Seven Kun Shen, and from Yancheng and Dajingtou they landed by separate routes and pressed toward Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw their full strength into the fight. Shibiao sent Commandant Lin Liang against Xigang while Brigade Commander Zhu Wen crossed the Seven Kun Shen shoals and landed from Yancheng and Dajingtou in separate columns toward Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 世驃督將士指揮布陣擊賊，賊潰，遂復台灣。

translations.literal: Shibiao directed officers and soldiers in array and struck the rebels; the rebels collapsed, and Taiwan was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao directed his officers in battle formation, the rebels collapsed, and Taiwan was recovered.

sentences.zh: 一貴走諸羅，諸羅民縛以獻，賊黨擒斬略盡。

translations.literal: Yigui fled to Zhuluo; the people of Zhuluo bound him and presented him; rebel partisans were captured and beheaded nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui fled to Zhuluo, where the locals bound him and handed him over. His followers were captured and executed almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 台灣南北兩路悉平。

translations.literal: The northern and southern routes of Taiwan were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Both the northern and southern routes of Taiwan were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔優敘，賜世驃東珠帽、黃帶、四團龍補服。

translations.literal: An edict gave him superior commendation and bestowed on Shibiao an eastern pearl cap, yellow belt, and four-clawed dragon surcoat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him with special honors and bestowed an eastern pearl cap, yellow belt, and four-clawed dragon surcoat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾卒於軍。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness in camp.

sentences.zh: 遺疏乞從父瑯葬福建，留妻子守墓，上悉許之。

translations.literal: His final memorial begged to be buried in Fujian with his father Lang and to leave his wife and children to tend the tomb; the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he asked to be buried in Fujian beside his father Lang and to leave his wife and children to tend the tomb. The emperor granted both requests.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，諡勇果。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Yongguo (Brave and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Yongguo, "Brave and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，世宗命予一等阿達哈哈番世職，以其子廷旉嗣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Yongzheng Emperor ordered that a first-class hereditary commandant of the A-da-ha-ha-fan be granted, with his son Tingyun to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng the emperor granted a first-class hereditary commandant's rank, which passed to his son Tingyun.

sentences.zh: 世驃和易謙雅，治軍嚴明。

translations.literal: Shibiao was easygoing, modest, and refined, and governed the army with strict clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao was affable, modest, and refined, and ran a strict, disciplined army.

sentences.zh: 與瑯先後平台灣，皆以六月乘海潮異漲渡師，遂以成功。

translations.literal: He and Lang pacified Taiwan in succession; both in the sixth month rode an extraordinary rise of the sea tide to ferry troops across, and thereby succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He and his father Lang conquered Taiwan in turn, each in the sixth month riding an extraordinary tidal surge to land their troops — and each thereby succeeded.

sentences.zh: 藍廷珍，字荊璞，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lan Tingzhen, style name Jingpu, was a man of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Tingzhen, whose style name was Jingpu, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少習騎射，從祖理器之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied mounted archery and followed his grandfather in managing armaments.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he trained in horsemanship and archery and assisted his grandfather in managing armaments.

sentences.zh: 入伍，自定海營把總累遷溫州鎮標左營游擊。

translations.literal: He entered military service, and from sergeant of the Dinghai garrison was promoted in succession to brigade commander of the Wenzhou garrison's Left Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army and rose from sergeant in the Dinghai garrison to brigade commander of the Wenzhou garrison's Left Battalion.

sentences.zh: 巡外洋，屢獲盜，盜皆畏避。

translations.literal: Patrolling the outer seas he repeatedly captured pirates, and pirates all feared and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: On patrol in the open sea he captured pirates again and again, until they all learned to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 以是為諸將所忌，讒於總督滿保，將劾之。

translations.literal: For this he was envied by other generals, who slandered him to Governor-General Manbao and were about to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals envied his success and slandered him to Governor-General Manbao, who was on the verge of impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 會關東大盜孫森等竊遼陽巨砲、戰艦逸入海。

translations.literal: It happened that the great Guandong bandit Sun Sen and others stole giant cannon and warships from Liaoyang and fled to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Guandong bandit Sun Sen and his gang stole heavy cannon and warships from Liaoyang and fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 聖祖震怒，責沿海疆吏嚴緝。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor was greatly angered and charged the coastal frontier officials to pursue them strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor was furious and ordered coastal officials to hunt them down without mercy.

sentences.zh: 廷珍出巡海，至黑水外洋與遇，力戰，盡獲森等九十餘人，及其船艦、砲械。

translations.literal: Tingzhen went out to patrol the sea, met them in the outer waters of Heishui, fought fiercely, and captured all of Sen and more than ninety men, together with their ships and artillery.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen put to sea, encountered them in the outer waters off Heishui, fought fiercely, and captured Sun Sen and more than ninety of his men along with their ships and guns.

sentences.zh: 滿保按部至溫州，廷珍迎謁以告。

translations.literal: When Manbao made his inspection tour to Wenzhou, Tingzhen met him and reported this.
translations.idiomatic: When Manbao arrived in Wenzhou on his inspection tour, Tingzhen met him and reported the victory.

sentences.zh: 滿保歎曰：「幾失良將！

translations.literal: Manbao sighed and said: "I nearly lost a fine general!
translations.idiomatic: Manbao sighed and said, "I nearly lost an excellent general!

sentences.zh: 」召入舟，厚撫之，亟疏薦，超擢福建澎湖副將。

translations.literal: "He summoned him aboard his boat, treated him generously, urgently memorialized to recommend him, and promoted him out of turn to Fujian Penghu deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Tingzhen aboard, treated him warmly, urgently recommended him in a memorial, and promoted him out of turn to deputy commander at Penghu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷南澳總兵。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Nan'ao regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Nan'ao.

sentences.zh: 六十年，硃一貴為亂，廷珍上書滿保策破賊狀，滿保令統戰船四百、將弁一百二十、官兵一萬二千，會提督施世驃於澎湖，剋期進剿。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Zhu Yigui rebelled; Tingzhen wrote to Manbao with a plan to defeat the rebels; Manbao ordered him to command four hundred warships, one hundred twenty officers, and twelve thousand soldiers, join Provincial Military Commissioner Shi Shibiao at Penghu, and advance on a fixed date.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year Zhu Yigui rebelled. Tingzhen sent Manbao a detailed plan for defeating the rebels. Manbao placed him in command of four hundred warships, one hundred twenty officers, and twelve thousand troops, ordered him to join Shi Shibiao at Penghu, and fixed a date for the assault.

sentences.zh: 廷珍至澎湖，言於世驃曰：「賊皆烏合，不足憂，惟脅從至三十萬人，請檄示止殲渠魁，餘勿問。

translations.literal: When Tingzhen reached Penghu he said to Shibiao: "The rebels are a rabble and not to be feared; only the coerced followers number as many as three hundred thousand — please issue a proclamation that only the ringleaders are to be destroyed and the rest not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: At Penghu Tingzhen told Shibiao: "The rebels are a rabble and not worth worrying over, but as many as three hundred thousand people were coerced into joining them. Issue a proclamation that only the ringleaders will be killed and the rest spared.

sentences.zh: 則人人有生之樂，無死之心，可不血刃平也。

translations.literal: Then every man will have the joy of life and no mind for death, and the land can be pacified without drawing swords."
translations.idiomatic: Then everyone will cling to life rather than court death, and the island can be pacified without bloodshed."

sentences.zh: 」世驃從之。

translations.literal: Shibiao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao agreed.

sentences.zh: 師至鹿耳門，賊扼險拒守。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luer Men the rebels held the strategic points and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Luer Men the rebels held the passes and resisted.

sentences.zh: 諸將林亮、董芳當前鋒，殊死戰，廷珍率大隊繼之，連戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Generals Lin Liang and Dong Fang served as vanguard and fought to the death; Tingzhen led the main force after them and won victory in successive battles.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Lin Liang and Dong Fang led the vanguard and fought desperately. Tingzhen followed with the main body and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 賊大潰，退保府治。

translations.literal: The rebels collapsed in great disorder and retreated to hold the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fell back to defend the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 世驃遣亮等自西港仔暗度，廷珍以大軍躡其後。

translations.literal: Shibiao sent Liang and others to cross secretly from Xigangzi; Tingzhen followed with the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao sent Liang and others to flank the enemy from Xigangzi while Tingzhen pressed forward with the main army.

sentences.zh: 賊在蘇厝甲，與亮等決戰，廷珍分兵馳赴之。

translations.literal: The rebels were at Sucuo Jia and fought a decisive battle with Liang and others; Tingzhen divided his troops and rushed to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels made a stand at Sucuo Jia and fought Liang's force to a decision. Tingzhen split his troops and hurried to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 賊望見旗幟，戰稍卻，乘勝追逐，遂大潰。

translations.literal: The rebels saw the banners and their fighting slackened; pursuing the victory they drove them to great collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing imperial banners the rebels faltered. The army pressed the advantage and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 夜駐犁頭標，設伏以待，賊果至，四面突擊，賊大亂，自相攻殺。

translations.literal: At night they encamped at Litou Biao and set an ambush; the rebels came as expected, were struck from four sides, fell into great disorder, and attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: That night they camped at Litou Biao and laid an ambush. When the rebels arrived as expected, troops struck from all sides. The rebels panicked and began killing one another.

sentences.zh: 追敗之木柵仔，复敗之蔦松溪，遂入府城，秋毫無所犯，民大悅。

translations.literal: Pursuing, they defeated them at Muzhaizi and again at Niaosong Stream, then entered the prefectural city without harming the slightest thing; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the rebels, defeated them at Muzhaizi and again at Niaosong Stream, and entered the prefectural city without harming a soul. The people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 一貴及其黨李勇、吳外等皆就擒。

translations.literal: Yigui and his partisans Li Yong, Wu Wai, and others were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui and his lieutenants Li Yong, Wu Wai, and others were all captured.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將復南北二路，署台灣總兵。

translations.literal: He dispatched generals to recover the northern and southern routes and acted as Taiwan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals to pacify the northern and southern routes and served as acting regional commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 秋，南路阿猴林餘孽復起，討平之。

translations.literal: In autumn remnants at Ahoulin on the southern route rose again and were suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn rebel remnants at Ahoulin on the southern route rose again and were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 招降陳福壽等十數人，皆渠魁也。

translations.literal: He induced the surrender of Chen Fushou and more than ten others, all ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the surrender of Chen Fushou and more than ten other ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 未幾，世驃卒，廷珍攝提督。

translations.literal: Before long Shibiao died and Tingzhen acted as provincial military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Shibiao died, and Tingzhen served as acting provincial military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 餘賊黃殿等以次擒滅。

translations.literal: Remaining rebels such as Huang Dian were captured and destroyed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels, including Huang Dian, were captured and eliminated one by one.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，授台灣總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he was appointed Taiwan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he was appointed regional commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，擢福建水師提督，加左都督，賜孔雀翎，予三等阿達哈哈番世職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was promoted to Fujian naval provincial military commissioner, given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief, bestowed a peacock feather, and granted a third-class hereditary commandant of the A-da-ha-ha-fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng he was promoted to provincial military commissioner of the Fujian naval forces, given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief, awarded a peacock feather, and granted a third-class hereditary commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗褒廷珍忠赤，惟屢勉以操守。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor praised Tingzhen's loyal devotion but repeatedly exhorted him on integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor praised Tingzhen's loyalty but repeatedly urged him to maintain his integrity.

sentences.zh: 二年，入覲，命赴馬蘭峪謁景陵，賞賚稠疊。

translations.literal: In the second year he came to audience, was ordered to go to Malanyu to pay respects at Jing Mausoleum, and received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he came to court, was sent to Malanyu to pay respects at the Jing Mausoleum, and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 七年，病聞，遣醫診視。

translations.literal: In the seventh year word of his illness came; physicians were sent to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year news of his illness reached the court, and physicians were sent to attend him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子少保，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: He soon died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xiangyi (Assisting and Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xiangyi, "Assisting and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 子日寵，嗣世職，官銅山營參將。

translations.literal: His son Richong succeeded to the hereditary office and served as garrison deputy commander of the Tongshan camp.
translations.idiomatic: His son Richong inherited the hereditary rank and served as deputy garrison commander of the Tongshan camp.

sentences.zh: 孫元枚，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Yuanmei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yuanmei has a biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 族弟鼎元，字玉霖，力學負才。

translations.literal: His clansman younger brother Ding Yuan, style name Yulin, studied hard and possessed talent.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman and younger cousin Ding Yuan, whose style name was Yulin, was a diligent scholar of exceptional ability.

sentences.zh: 廷珍統師入台灣，鼎元參軍事，著平台紀略。

translations.literal: When Tingzhen commanded the army into Taiwan, Ding Yuan assisted in military affairs and wrote A Brief Account of Pacifying Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhen led the army into Taiwan, Ding Yuan served on his staff and wrote A Brief Account of Pacifying Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔舉文行兼優之士，貢入太學，有司以鼎元薦，大學士硃軾器之，用薦得召見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict called for men of both literary and moral excellence to be presented to the Imperial Academy; the local officials recommended Ding Yuan; Grand Secretary Zhu Fachi valued him, and through recommendation he was summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict called for scholars of both learning and character to enter the Imperial Academy. Local officials recommended Ding Yuan, Grand Secretary Zhu Fachi took notice of him, and he was summoned to audience on that recommendation.

sentences.zh: 上書陳時政，上嘉納。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on current policy and the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, which the emperor praised and adopted.

sentences.zh: 授廣東普寧知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Puning in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Puning in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 居官有惠政，長於斷獄。

translations.literal: In office he had benevolent policies and excelled at deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he governed with kindness and was especially skilled at adjudicating cases.

sentences.zh: 性伉直，坐事劾罷。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and unyielding; for an affair he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and uncompromising by nature, he was impeached and dismissed over a dispute.

sentences.zh: 總督鄂彌達白其誣，召詣京師。

translations.literal: Governor-General E'erchidao reported that he had been falsely charged and he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General E'erchidao reported that the charges were false, and he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 旋署廣州知府。

translations.literal: He was soon made acting prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，卒。

translations.literal: After only one month he died.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he died.

sentences.zh: 鼎元嘗論台灣善後策，謂諸羅宜畫地更設一縣，總兵不可移駐澎湖。

translations.literal: Ding Yuan once discussed policies for Taiwan's aftermath, saying Zhuluo should be divided to establish another county and the regional commander should not be moved to garrison Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Yuan once proposed a postwar plan for Taiwan: Zhuluo should be divided to form a new county, and the regional commander should not be stationed at Penghu.

sentences.zh: 後諸羅析縣曰彰化，更設北路三營，總兵官仍駐台灣，皆如鼎元言。

translations.literal: Later Zhuluo was split into a county called Zhanghua, three northern-route camps were newly established, and the regional commander still garrisoned Taiwan — all as Ding Yuan had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhuluo was divided to form Zhanghua County, three northern garrisons were established, and the regional commander remained stationed in Taiwan — all as Ding Yuan had urged.

sentences.zh: 林亮，字漢侯，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lin Liang, style name Hanhou, was a man of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Liang, whose style name was Hanhou, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 少習騎射擊刺。

translations.literal: In youth he studied mounted archery and close combat.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he trained in horsemanship, archery, and close combat.

sentences.zh: 生長海濱，島澳險夷，舟航利鈍，靡不講求。

translations.literal: Growing up on the coast he studied every island and harbor's dangers and ease, and the advantages and drawbacks of shipping.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on the coast, he mastered every island harbor's hazards, currents, and the strengths and weaknesses of each route.

sentences.zh: 初授台灣水師把總，累遷澎湖協守備。

translations.literal: He was first appointed sergeant of the Taiwan naval forces and was promoted in succession to Penghu garrison commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a naval sergeant in Taiwan and rose to commandant of the Penghu garrison.

sentences.zh: 硃一貴陷台灣，官吏渡澎湖，居民洶懼。

translations.literal: When Zhu Yigui seized Taiwan, officials crossed to Penghu and the inhabitants were in uproar and fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yigui overran Taiwan, officials fled to Penghu and the populace panicked.

sentences.zh: 將吏以孤島難守，僉議撤歸廈門，各遣家屬登舟。

translations.literal: Officers, finding the isolated island hard to defend, unanimously debated withdrawing to Xiamen and each sent their families aboard ship.
translations.idiomatic: The officers, deeming the isolated island indefensible, voted to withdraw to Xiamen and began sending their families aboard ship.

sentences.zh: 亮按劍厲聲曰：「朝廷疆土，尺寸不可棄！

translations.literal: Liang grasped his sword and said in a stern voice: "The empire's territory — not an inch may be abandoned!
translations.idiomatic: Liang gripped his sword and declared in a thunderous voice: "This is imperial territory — not an inch may be abandoned!

sentences.zh: 今鋒刃未血，相率委去，縱避賊刃，能逃國法乎？

translations.literal: Now before blades have drawn blood you would all abandon your posts together — even if you escape the rebels' blades, can you escape the nation's law?"
translations.idiomatic: Before a single blade has been blooded you would abandon your posts? Even if you escape the rebels, can you escape the law?"

sentences.zh: 請整兵配船，守禦要害，賊至，決死戰！

translations.literal: I ask that troops be arrayed and ships assigned, key points defended — when rebels come, fight to the death!"
translations.idiomatic: Muster the troops, assign the ships, and hold the key positions. When the rebels come, we fight to the death!"

sentences.zh: 戰不捷，亮死，君等去未遲。

translations.literal: If the battle is not won, Liang dies — you gentlemen may leave then and it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If we lose, I die first — then you may withdraw, and it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」乃馳赴海口，申號令，驅將吏家屬登岸，令敢言退廈門者斬。

translations.literal: He then galloped to the harbor mouth, proclaimed orders, drove officers' families ashore, and ordered that whoever dared speak of retreating to Xiamen be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to the harbor, issued his orders, drove the officers' families back ashore, and decreed death for anyone who spoke of retreating to Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 時糧絕餉匱，亮輸貲買穀，碾米給軍，制戰攻器械，俟師至。

translations.literal: At the time grain and pay were exhausted; Liang contributed his own wealth to buy grain, milled rice to supply the army, made weapons for attack, and awaited the main force.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies had run out. Liang spent his own money to buy grain, milled rice for the troops, forged weapons, and waited for the main army.

sentences.zh: 提督施世驃、總兵藍廷珍以亮忠勇，令當前鋒，領舟師五百七十人抵鹿耳門。

translations.literal: Provincial Military Commissioner Shi Shibiao and Regional Commander Lan Tingzhen, for Liang's loyalty and courage, made him vanguard leading five hundred seventy men of the fleet to Luer Men.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shibiao and Lan Tingzhen, impressed by Liang's loyalty and courage, made him vanguard with five hundred seventy sailors at Luer Men.

sentences.zh: 一貴黨蘇天威據砲台以拒，亮率六艦直進，發砲中敵，火起，斃賊無算。

translations.literal: Yigui's partisan Su Tianwei held the batteries to resist; Liang led six ships straight in, fired cannon that struck the enemy, flames rose, and countless rebels were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui's follower Su Tianwei held the batteries. Liang led six ships straight in, his cannon struck home, flames erupted, and countless rebels fell.

sentences.zh: 乘勝進攻安平鎮，亮先登樹幟，賊潰走。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he attacked Anping Town; Liang was first to ascend and raise the banner, and the rebels fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage he assaulted Anping. Liang was first ashore to raise the imperial banner, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 翌日，鏖戰鯤身，駕舟橫衝賊陣，復大敗之。

translations.literal: The next day he fought fiercely at Kun Shen, drove his boat across the rebel formation, and again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fought a fierce battle at Kun Shen, drove his vessel straight through the rebel line, and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 賊退至府城，世驃令亮分兵自西港仔暗度拊其背，廷珍以軍繼進，大戰，賊死傷遍野，遂克府治。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated to the prefectural city; Shibiao ordered Liang to divide troops and cross secretly from Xigangzi to strike their rear; Tingzhen followed with the army; in a great battle rebel dead and wounded covered the fields, and the prefectural seat was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fell back on the prefectural city. Shibiao ordered Liang to flank them from Xigangzi while Tingzhen pressed forward. In the great battle rebel dead and wounded covered the plain, and the prefectural seat fell.

sentences.zh: 亮功最，遷台灣參將。

translations.literal: Liang's merit was greatest and he was transferred to Taiwan deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's achievements were foremost, and he was promoted to deputy commander in Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，敘平台灣功，加都督同知，予一等阿達哈哈番世職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, recounting the merit of pacifying Taiwan, he was given the additional rank of Vice Commander-in-Chief and granted a first-class hereditary commandant of the A-da-ha-ha-fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng his role in pacifying Taiwan was recognized with the additional rank of Vice Commander-in-Chief and a first-class hereditary commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，入京，上深嘉之，擢水師副將，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: That autumn he entered the capital; the emperor deeply praised him, promoted him to naval deputy commander, and bestowed a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he went to the capital, won the emperor's high praise, was promoted to naval deputy commander, and received a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二年，授台灣鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed regional commander of the Taiwan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed regional commander of the Taiwan garrison.

sentences.zh: 亮以台灣初被兵，加意撫綏，整水陸兵防。

translations.literal: As Taiwan had just suffered warfare, Liang gave special attention to pacification and reorganized land and sea defenses.
translations.idiomatic: With Taiwan just emerging from war, Liang devoted himself to pacification and reorganized the land and naval defenses.

sentences.zh: 又招撫生番一百八社、男婦一萬八百餘人。

translations.literal: He also induced the submission of one hundred eight aboriginal communities, more than ten thousand eight hundred men and women.
translations.idiomatic: He also won over one hundred eight aboriginal communities, totaling more than ten thousand eight hundred men and women.

sentences.zh: 亮因番嗜色布、鹽、糖，遣吏歷各社齎賜之，因宣布德意，群番悅服。

translations.literal: As the aborigines loved colored cloth, salt, and sugar, Liang sent officials through each community to present gifts, proclaimed the court's benevolence, and all the communities submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the aborigines valued colored cloth, salt, and sugar, he sent officials to every community with gifts, proclaimed the court's benevolence, and won their willing submission.

sentences.zh: 五年，移浙江定海，卒於官，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Dinghai in Zhejiang, died in office, and was granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Dinghai in Zhejiang, died in office, and was granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 何勉，字尚敏，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: He Mian, style name Shangmin, was a man of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He Mian, whose style name was Shangmin, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初授督標把總。

translations.literal: He was first appointed sergeant of the governor's standard garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a sergeant in the governor's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十八年，薛彥文等聚後洋山為匪，勉奉檄捕擒之。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year of Kangxi Xue Yanwen and others gathered at Houyang Mountain as bandits; Mian received orders and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year of Kangxi, Xue Yanwen and others formed a band at Houyang Mountain. Mian received orders, pursued them, and captured them.

sentences.zh: 六十年，從提督施世驃討硃一貴，勉攻南路，擒其黨杜會三、蘇清等；

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he followed Provincial Military Commissioner Shi Shibiao in suppressing Zhu Yigui; Mian attacked the southern route and captured partisans Du Huisan, Su Qing, and others;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he followed Shi Shibiao against Zhu Yigui, attacked the southern route, and captured the rebels Du Huisan, Su Qing, and others;

sentences.zh: 又於北路獲黃潛等二十六人。

translations.literal: on the northern route he also seized Huang Qian and twenty-six others.
translations.idiomatic: on the northern route he also seized Huang Qian and twenty-six others.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷台灣鎮標千總。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to sergeant-major of the Taiwan garrison standard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to sergeant-major of the Taiwan garrison.

sentences.zh: 時一貴餘黨王忠等出沒內山，巡視台灣御史吳達禮督捕治，總兵藍廷珍檄勉偵緝。

translations.literal: At the time Yigui's remaining partisans Wang Zhong and others appeared and vanished in the inner mountains; Taiwan touring censor Wu Dali supervised pursuit; regional commander Lan Tingzhen ordered Mian to scout and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui's remaining followers, including Wang Zhong, were hiding in the inner mountains. Touring censor Wu Dali of Taiwan supervised the hunt, and Lan Tingzhen ordered Mian to track them down.

sentences.zh: 遣降卒為導，入鳳山深箐中，獲賊黨劉富生，思拒捕，立擒之。

translations.literal: He sent surrendered soldiers as guides, entered the deep ravines of Fengshan, captured the rebel partisan Liu Fusheng, who thought to resist arrest, and seized him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Using surrendered soldiers as guides, he penetrated the deep ravines of Fengshan, found the rebel Liu Fusheng, and seized him the moment he tried to resist.

sentences.zh: 擢北路營參將，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Northern Route Camp and granted a hereditary commandant of the Tuo-shali-ha-fan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Northern Route Camp and granted a hereditary commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，水連沙等社叛番蠢動，總督高其倬檄從台灣道吳昌祚按治。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng the rebellious aborigines of Shuilian Sha and other communities stirred; Governor-General Gao Qisuo ordered him to follow Taiwan Circuit Intendant Wu Changzuo in pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongzheng the Shuilian Sha communities and other rebel aborigines rose up. Governor-General Gao Qisuo ordered him to assist Taiwan Circuit Intendant Wu Changzuo in suppressing them.

sentences.zh: 勉攻北港，番請降，水連沙二十五社悉平。

translations.literal: Mian attacked Beigang; the aborigines begged to surrender, and all twenty-five communities of Shuilian Sha were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Mian attacked Beigang. The aborigines sued for peace, and all twenty-five Shuilian Sha communities were pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣洞庭協副將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander of the Dongting garrison in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy commander of the Dongting garrison in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十年，貴州九股苗作亂，詔發湖廣兵二千協剿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Jiugu Miao of Guizhou rebelled; an edict dispatched two thousand Huguang troops to assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Jiugu Miao of Guizhou rebelled, and an edict sent two thousand troops from Huguang to assist in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 提督張正興檄勉領兵五百赴貴州，進攻交汪寨。

translations.literal: Provincial Military Commissioner Zhang Zhengxing ordered Mian to lead five hundred troops to Guizhou and attack Jiaowang Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Military Commissioner Zhang Zhengxing ordered Mian to lead five hundred men to Guizhou and assault Jiaowang Stockade.

sentences.zh: 勉乘霧夾擊，苗敗遁，复據蓮花峰築屯。

translations.literal: Mian took advantage of fog to strike from both sides; the Miao were defeated and fled, then again held Lianhua Peak and built a stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Mian struck through the fog from both flanks. The Miao fled, then regrouped on Lianhua Peak and built a fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 時貴州提督哈元生自台拱移軍至，令勉攻其東。

translations.literal: At that time Guizhou Provincial Military Commissioner Ha Yuansheng moved his army from Taigong and ordered Mian to attack the east.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Provincial Military Commissioner Ha Yuansheng then arrived from Taigong and ordered Mian to attack from the east.

sentences.zh: 勉先登奪，賊竄走，掩擊之，陣斬其渠，餘眾就擒。

translations.literal: Mian was first to ascend and seize the stockade; the rebels scattered in flight; he pursued and struck them, beheaded their leader in battle, and the rest were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was first to storm the stockade. The rebels scattered, he pursued and struck them down, killed their leader in battle, and captured the rest.

sentences.zh: 擢雲南鶴麗鎮總兵，調臨元，復調廣東左翼。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regional commander of Heli garrison in Yunnan, transferred to Linyuan, and again transferred to the Left Wing of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regional commander at Heli in Yunnan, transferred to Linyuan, and later to the Left Wing command in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 五年，調台灣，尋又移南澳，署福建水師提督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Taiwan, soon moved to Nan'ao, and acted as Fujian naval provincial military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Taiwan, soon to Nan'ao, and served as acting provincial military commissioner of the Fujian naval forces.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年，以疾乞休，詔解任回籍調治。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong he begged retirement on account of illness; an edict released him from office to return home for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qianlong he requested retirement due to illness and was released to return home for treatment.

sentences.zh: 尋召詣京師，以篤老，命原品休致。

translations.literal: He was soon summoned to the capital; because of advanced age he was ordered to retire with his original rank preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to the capital, but because of his advanced age was permitted to retire at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died and was granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year and was granted state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 子思和，嗣世職。

translations.literal: His son Sihe succeeded to the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sihe inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，复官台灣總兵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he again held office as Taiwan regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he again served as regional commander of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 陳倫蜅，字次安，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Chen Lunjiong, style name Ci'an, was a man of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lunjiong, whose style name was Ci'an, was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父昂，字英士，弱冠賈海上，習島嶼形勢、風潮險易。

translations.literal: His father Ang, style name Yingshi, in his early twenties traded on the sea and learned the configurations of islands, and the dangers and ease of winds and tides.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen Ang, whose style name was Yingshi, took to maritime trade in his youth and mastered island geography, winds, tides, and every hazard of the sea.

sentences.zh: 施琅徵台灣，徵從軍，有功，授游擊。

translations.literal: When Shi Lang campaigned against Taiwan, Ang was recruited to follow the army, performed merit, and was appointed brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Lang campaigned against Taiwan, Ang joined his forces, distinguished himself, and was appointed brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷至碣石總兵，擢廣東右翼副都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to regional commander of Jieshi and elevated to deputy commander of the Right Wing in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regional commander of Jieshi and was promoted to deputy commander of the Right Wing in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏言：「西洋治曆法者宜定員，毋多留，留者勿使布教。

translations.literal: He once memorialized: "Westerners who manage the calendar should have a fixed quota, not many kept; those kept should not be allowed to spread religion."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized: "Westerners employed in calendrical work should be kept to a fixed quota, not in large numbers, and those retained must not be allowed to proselytize."

sentences.zh: 」又以沿海居民困於海禁，將疏請弛之。

translations.literal: He also, because coastal residents suffered under the maritime prohibition, was about to memorialize requesting its relaxation.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to memorialize for easing the maritime prohibition, which had burdened coastal residents.

sentences.zh: 會疾作，命倫蜅以遺疏進，詔報可。

translations.literal: When illness came on he ordered Lunjiong to submit the final memorial; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he had Lunjiong submit the memorial on his behalf, and the emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 倫蜅初以廕生授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: Lunjiong was first appointed a third-rank bodyguard by hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Lunjiong began as a third-rank imperial bodyguard through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，授台灣總兵，調廣東高廉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was appointed Taiwan regional commander and transferred to Gaolian in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was appointed regional commander of Taiwan, then transferred to Gaolian in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 坐事降台灣副將。

translations.literal: For an affair he was demoted to Taiwan deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to deputy commander in Taiwan after a disciplinary case.

sentences.zh: 复授總兵，歷江南蘇松、狼山諸鎮。

translations.literal: He was again appointed regional commander and served in succession at Sushong and Langshan garrisons in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed regional commander and served at the Sushong and Langshan garrisons in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Zhejiang provincial military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial military commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 昂疏並言：「臣詳察海上諸國，東海日本為大，次則琉球。

translations.literal: Ang also said in his memorial: "Your servant has closely examined the countries of the sea: in the eastern sea Japan is greatest, next Ryukyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's memorial also stated: "I have closely examined the maritime powers. In the eastern seas Japan is foremost, followed by Ryukyu.

sentences.zh: 西則暹羅為最。

translations.literal: To the west Siam is foremost.
translations.idiomatic: To the west Siam is the strongest.

sentences.zh: 東南番族文萊等數十小國，惟噶囉吧、呂宋最強。

translations.literal: Among the southeastern barbarian states Brunei and dozens of small countries — only Kalapa and Luzon are strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Among the southeastern states, Brunei and dozens of smaller kingdoms — only Kalapa and Luzon are truly powerful.

sentences.zh: 噶囉吧為紅毛一種，中有英圭黎、干絲蠛、和蘭西、荷蘭、大小西洋各國。

translations.literal: Kalapa belongs to the Red-Hair race, including among them England, Castile, France, Holland, and the countries of the greater and lesser Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Kalapa is home to the Westerners, including the English, Castilians, French, Dutch, and other nations of the Atlantic world.

sentences.zh: 和蘭西最凶狠，與澳門種人同派，習廣東情事。

translations.literal: The French are most fierce and cruel, of the same stock as the people at Macau, and versed in Guangdong affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The French are the most aggressive, kin to the Macanese, and well acquainted with Guangdong affairs.

sentences.zh: 請敕督、撫、關差諸臣防備，於未入港之先，取其火砲。

translations.literal: I ask that governors, provincial officials, and customs officers be ordered to take precautions and seize their cannon before they enter harbor.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that governors, provincial officials, and customs officers be ordered to seize foreign cannon before ships enter port.

sentences.zh: 另設所關束，每年不許多船並集。

translations.literal: Separate stations should be established to restrain them, and each year many ships must not be allowed to gather together.
translations.idiomatic: Separate customs stations should be established, and large fleets must not be allowed to congregate in port each year.

sentences.zh: 」下兵部，但令沿海將吏晝夜防衛，寢昂議。

translations.literal: "It was sent to the Ministry of War, which only ordered coastal generals and officials to guard day and night, and Ang's proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of War, which merely ordered coastal officers to maintain round-the-clock vigilance and set Ang's proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 倫蜅為侍衛時，聖祖嘗召詢互市諸國事，對悉與圖籍合。

translations.literal: When Lunjiong was a bodyguard the Sacred Ancestor once summoned him to inquire about the countries engaged in tribute trade; his answers all matched the maps and records.
translations.idiomatic: When Lunjiong served as a bodyguard, the Kangxi Emperor once questioned him about the tribute-trade nations, and his answers matched the official maps and records in every detail.

sentences.zh: 時互市諸國奉約束惟謹，獨昂、倫蜅父子有遠慮，憂之最早雲。

translations.literal: At the time the tribute-trade countries observed restrictions with utmost care; only Ang and the father-and-son Lunjiong had far-sighted concern and worried earliest of all.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the trading nations observed every restriction, yet only Ang and his son Lunjiong looked ahead with foreboding — they were the first to worry.

sentences.zh: 歐陽凱，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Kai, a man of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Kai was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 起行伍，累官江南蘇松水師營總兵。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and was promoted in succession to regional commander of the Sushong naval camp in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become regional commander of the Sushong naval camp in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年，調福建台灣鎮，以功加左都督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Taiwan garrison in Fujian and for merit was given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi he was transferred to the Taiwan garrison in Fujian and given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief for his service.

sentences.zh: 六十年，硃一貴作亂，官軍遇賊於赤山，千總陳元戰死。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Zhu Yigui rebelled; government troops met the rebels at Chishan and sergeant-major Chen Yuan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year Zhu Yigui rebelled. Government troops met the rebels at Chishan, where Sergeant-Major Chen Yuan fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 賊進攻鳳山，把總林富戰死，守備馬定國自殺。

translations.literal: The rebels advanced on Fengshan; sergeant Lin Fu died in battle and commandant Ma Dingguo killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked Fengshan. Sergeant Lin Fu was killed in battle, and Commandant Ma Dingguo took his own life.

sentences.zh: 凱率所部守備胡忠義、千總蔣子龍、把總林彥御之春牛埔；

translations.literal: Kai led his commandants Hu Zhongyi, sergeant-major Jiang Zilong, and sergeant Lin Yan to defend Chunniu Po;
translations.idiomatic: Kai led his officers — Commandant Hu Zhongyi, Sergeant-Major Jiang Zilong, and Sergeant Lin Yan — to defend Chunniu Po;

sentences.zh: 參將羅萬倉，游擊孫文元，城守游擊許雲，守備遊崇功，千總趙奇奉、林文煌，把總李茂吉率水師來會，力戰破賊。

translations.literal: deputy commander Luo Wancang, brigade commander Sun Wenyuan, garrison brigade commander Xu Yun, commandant You Chonggong, sergeant-majors Zhao Qifeng and Lin Wenhuan, and sergeant Li Maoji led the naval forces to join them and fought fiercely to defeat the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Luo Wancang, Brigade Commander Sun Wenyuan, Garrison Brigade Commander Xu Yun, Commandant You Chonggong, Sergeant-Majors Zhao Qifeng and Lin Wenhuan, and Sergeant Li Maoji brought the fleet to join them and fought fiercely to rout the rebels.

sentences.zh: 次日，賊大至，凱力戰，與忠義子龍彥俱沒於陣，賊截凱首去。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels came in great force; Kai fought desperately and perished in battle together with Zhongyi, Zilong, and Yan; the rebels cut off Kai's head and took it away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels returned in force. Kai fought to the end and fell with Zhongyi, Zilong, and Yan. The rebels severed Kai's head and carried it away.

sentences.zh: 雲、崇功、奇奉、文煌同日戰死。

translations.literal: Yun, Chonggong, Qifeng, and Wenhuan all died in battle on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun, You Chonggong, Zhao Qifeng, and Lin Wenhuan all died in battle that same day.

sentences.zh: 茂吉被執，不屈，死。

translations.literal: Maoji was captured, refused to submit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Maoji was captured, refused to yield, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 賊陷府治，萬倉戰死，文元奔鹿耳門投海死。

translations.literal: The rebels seized the prefectural seat; Wancang died in battle; Wenyuan fled to Luer Men and threw himself into the sea to die.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels overran the prefectural seat. Wancang fell in battle, and Wenyuan fled to Luer Men and drowned himself in the sea.

sentences.zh: 同死者游擊王九人、守備吳泰嵩。

translations.literal: Who died with them were brigade commander Wang and nine others and commandant Wu Taisong.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Wang and nine others and Commandant Wu Taisong also died.

sentences.zh: 又有把總石琳，自汀州被檄至台灣，遇變被圍，死之。

translations.literal: There was also sergeant Shi Lin, summoned from Tingzhou to Taiwan, who when the crisis came was surrounded and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sergeant Shi Lin had also been summoned from Tingzhou to Taiwan; when the uprising broke out he was surrounded and killed.

sentences.zh: 六月，師克台灣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the army recovered Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month imperial forces recovered Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 一貴既誅，獲其黨黃殿等，械送福州獄。

translations.literal: After Yigui was executed, his partisans Huang Dian and others were captured and sent in shackles to prison in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yigui was executed, his followers Huang Dian and others were captured and sent in chains to prison in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年二月，賊破械斬關出，至下渡尾，都司閻威、守備楊士虎逐捕，殺數賊，被創死。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yongzheng the prisoners broke their shackles, cut through the gate, and fled to Xiaduwei; brigade commander Yan Wei and commandant Yang Shihu pursued them, killed several rebels, and died of wounds received.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yongzheng the prisoners broke their chains, cut through the gate, and fled to Xiaduwei. Brigade Commander Yan Wei and Commandant Yang Shihu pursued them, killed several rebels, and died of their wounds.

sentences.zh: 先後議卹，凱贈太子少保，廕守備；

translations.literal: Posthumous honors were deliberated in succession; Kai was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with a hereditary commandant's privilege;
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors were granted in turn. Kai was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent posthumously, with a hereditary privilege for a commandant's rank;

sentences.zh: 雲以下皆贈官、予世職有差。

translations.literal: Yun and those below were all given posthumous offices and hereditary ranks in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yun and the others received posthumous offices and hereditary ranks in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 羅萬倉，甘肅寧夏人。

translations.literal: Luo Wancang, a man of Ningxia in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Wancang was a native of Ningxia in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 官北路參將。

translations.literal: He held office as deputy commander of the Northern Route.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy commander of the Northern Route.

sentences.zh: 凱戰死，賊攻府城，萬倉督將卒登埤，發大砲擊賊，僕賊旗。

translations.literal: When Kai died in battle the rebels attacked the prefectural city; Wancang directed officers and soldiers onto the ramparts, fired great cannon at the rebels, and knocked down their banners.
translations.idiomatic: After Kai's death the rebels assaulted the prefectural city. Wancang directed his men onto the walls, fired heavy cannon, and shot down the rebel banners.

sentences.zh: 賊大至，萬倉出城與戰，逾溝墜馬，賊以竹篙刺其喉，猶揮刀殺賊乃死。

translations.literal: The rebels came in great force; Wancang went out of the city to fight, crossed a ditch and fell from his horse; rebels stabbed his throat with bamboo poles, yet he still swung his blade and killed rebels before he died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came in overwhelming numbers. Wancang rode out to fight, fell from his horse crossing a ditch, and was stabbed in the throat with bamboo poles — yet he still swung his blade and killed several rebels before he died.

sentences.zh: 妾蔣聞報，自經殉。

translations.literal: His concubine Jiang, hearing the report, hanged herself in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news, his concubine Jiang hanged herself in devotion.

sentences.zh: 遊崇功，字仲嘉，福建漳浦人。

translations.literal: You Chonggong, style name Zhongjia, was a man of Zhangpu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: You Chonggong, whose style name was Zhongjia, was a native of Zhangpu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 材力雄健。
